evals.prompt:
Build a UDF that flags hydraulic pressure readings outside a safe operating band, using the Time Series Analytics microservice at microservices/time-series-analytics. Field `pressure_bar` arrives via POST /input; flag any reading below 80 or above 150. Name the UDF `pressure_guard`. Deploy it against a running instance of the service and confirm flagged points show up in the container logs.

Validate using the prebuilt intel/ia-time-series-analytics-microservice image via Docker Compose, and these sample input points: {"topic": "point_data", "fields": {"pressure_bar": 65}} (should flag) and {"topic": "point_data", "fields": {"pressure_bar": 110}} (should not flag).
evals.expected_output: A pressure_guard UDF + tick script + tar package, deployed and actively flagging the 65 bar point while not flagging the 110 bar point.
expectations: A UDF file named pressure_guard.py exists implementing threshold detection logic
A tick script named pressure_guard.tick exists and its UDF node invokes @pressure_guard()
The deployment package was successfully uploaded via POST /udfs/package (not just written locally)
Config was successfully applied naming udfs.name as pressure_guard via POST /config
Sending pressure_bar=65 produces a flagged/logged anomaly in the container logs
Sending pressure_bar=110 does NOT produce a flagged anomaly in the container logs
The UDF reads the pressure_bar field specifically, not a different or generic field name

evals.prompt:
Build a UDF that detects sudden vibration spikes on a motor and publishes an MQTT alert when one occurs, using the Time Series Analytics microservice at microservices/time-series-analytics. Field `vibration_mm_s` arrives via POST /input; flag a point if it jumps more than 5 mm/s from the previous reading. Wire the flagged output to an MQTT alert assuming the broker is named `motor_alerts_broker`. Name the UDF `vibration_spike_detector`.

Validate using the prebuilt intel/ia-time-series-analytics-microservice image via Docker Compose, with MQTT alerting configured. Send this sequence to POST /input: vibration_mm_s = 2.0, then 2.1, then 9.5 (the jump from 2.1 to 9.5 should flag), then 9.6 (should not flag -- small delta from the now-elevated baseline).
evals.expected_output: A vibration_spike_detector UDF that tracks the previous reading across calls, only flags the 2.1 -> 9.5 jump, and a tick script wired to Kapacitor's native MQTT alert node for broker `motor_alerts_broker`.
expectations: A UDF file named vibration_spike_detector.py exists that tracks a previous value across point() calls as instance state
A tick script named vibration_spike_detector.tick exists that references the vibration_spike_detector UDF node
The tick script includes an alert node configured for MQTT broker motor_alerts_broker (not just a bare UDF node)
The deployment package was successfully uploaded and config applied via the REST API
Sending the sequence 2.0, 2.1, 9.5 results in the 9.5 point being flagged (delta from 2.1 exceeds 5 mm/s)
Sending 9.6 immediately after 9.5 does NOT get flagged (small delta from the now-elevated baseline)
The rate-of-change threshold used is 5 mm/s as specified, not an arbitrary different value

evals.prompt:
Deploy a pretrained anomaly-detection model for wind turbine sensor data through the Time Series Analytics microservice at microservices/time-series-analytics. A scikit-learn model (windturbine_anomaly_detector.pkl, an IsolationForest trained on a single numeric field) is provided as an input file -- wire it up for per-point inference rather than writing new detection logic. Name the UDF `windturbine_anomaly_detector`; the model file should be referenced in the deployment config, device set to CPU.

Validate using the prebuilt intel/ia-time-series-analytics-microservice image via Docker Compose. Send a normal-range reading (e.g. field value 50) and an extreme outlier (e.g. field value 200) via POST /input and confirm only the outlier is flagged.
evals.expected_output: A windturbine_anomaly_detector UDF that loads the provided model once and calls .predict() per point, correctly distinguishing the normal reading from the outlier.
expectations: A UDF file named windturbine_anomaly_detector.py exists that loads the provided .pkl model once in __init__ (or equivalent), not per-point
The deployment package includes the PROVIDED windturbine_anomaly_detector.pkl file, not a newly trained model
The config applied via POST /config references the model file under udfs.models and sets udfs.device to CPU
Sending a normal-range reading (value near 50) does not get flagged
Sending an outlier reading (value 200) gets flagged
The UDF calls model.predict() and treats -1 as the anomaly convention consistent with IsolationForest
